svg.text: D · Shift report — what the depot sees
The driver is not the only user. Across drivers and weeks, the log becomes scheduling data — and rostering is the actual fix for fatigue.
1 · From log to report
session_log.csv
one row every 3 seconds
AGGREGATE THE SHIFT
· smooth the score to a trend line
· find the worst continuous stretch
· count alerts by level
Enough valid data?
< 60% full mode → flag the report
ONE-PAGE SHIFT REPORT
generated automatically at shift end
goes to driver and to depot
Two readers, two different documents
The driver's copy is about today: how the shift went,
when the hard stretch was, whether the breaks helped.
It is feedback, not a report card.
The depot's copy is about patterns across people and
weeks. No individual driver is the subject — the
roster is.
Flag incomplete reports honestly
A shift spent largely in degraded mode produced less
information, not better numbers. If the system could
not see the driver for half the drive, the report
must say so rather than quietly reporting a low
fatigue score that only means "no data".
Privacy by construction
The log holds a profile label and numbers about blink
timing. No video is stored, no face is recognised,
nothing identifies a person. Fleet monitoring is often
resented; one that cannot identify anyone is different.
2 · The driver's page
FATIGUE SCORE OVER THE SHIFT
alert level
WORST STRETCH
12:10 – 12:40, sustained above threshold
Driven by blink reopen slowdown and
three hand-to-face events.
Recovered after the 12:45 stop.
ALERTS AND LEAD TIME
mild
moderate
severe
First early signal preceded the first
late signal by 6 min 20 s.
Feedback, not surveillance
The driver sees their own page first, before anyone
else does. That ordering matters for whether the
system gets accepted or quietly sabotaged.
Showing the lead time is the part drivers find
persuasive. "The system noticed six minutes before
you did" is a concrete demonstration that the early
signals are real and not theatre.
Show recovery, not just decline
Marking where a break brought the score back down
turns the report into something actionable. It also
gives you the beginnings of an answer to the question
nobody asks: does the intervention actually work?
3 · The depot's page
FATIGUE EVENTS BY SHIFT SLOT
THE FINDING
The 02:00 slot produces roughly three
times the fatigue events of any other,
across all drivers.
That is a rostering problem, not a
ALSO VISIBLE
· which routes produce the most events
· whether back-to-back shifts compound
· whether break length changes recovery
· how often the system ran degraded,
i.e. where the data is weak
This is where the real value sits
An alert treats the symptom. The roster is the cause.
A depot manager currently has no way to know that
their 2am slot is three times worse than any other,
because nobody measures fatigue systematically. Once
they can see it, they can change the schedule — which
prevents fatigue instead of warning about it.
Aggregate, never rank individuals
The depot view should be by slot, route and week —
not a leaderboard of drivers. A system that ranks
people by tiredness will be gamed within a week, and
the gaming will make the data useless. Design the
view so there is nothing to game.
4 · Build cost
WHAT IT TAKES
pandas to group the log
matplotlib for two charts
a Markdown or HTML template
Roughly two days.
WHAT IT GIVES THE PROJECT
· a second thing to show in the demo
besides the alarm going off
· a reason the system is worth
deploying, not just worth building
· a report section nobody else has
HONEST LIMITATION
RLDD gives you ten-minute clips, not
eight-hour shifts. You can build and
demonstrate the report, but you cannot
validate the slot findings. Say so.
DEMO WORKAROUND
Concatenate clips into a synthetic
"shift" and label it as synthetic.
What to claim and what not to
Claim: the system produces a shift report, and the
aggregation is demonstrated on synthetic shifts built
from the dataset.
Do not claim: that the 2am finding is real. You have
no overnight fleet data, and inventing the number
would be the one thing that sinks an otherwise
honest project.
Present the depot page as a designed capability with
illustrative data, clearly marked. That is a normal
and respectable thing to do, and an examiner will
read it as scope awareness rather than a gap.
Validating it on real fleet data goes in future work.
